**Headline (top section):**
Why you keep *waking* at 3am

**Body paragraphs (middle section, staggered):**
It's not random. That early morning cortisol spike is your nervous system signalling it's stuck in fight-or-flight, even though you're lying in bed.

We see this pattern constantly in the clinic — usually because your parasympathetic brake isn't engaging at night. Your vagal tone has dropped, and your body has learned to treat sleep as unsafe.

The fix isn't a supplement or a sleep hack. It's a nervous-system reset your body recognises instantly.

Gargle water hard for 30 seconds before bed. Cold water works best. You're stimulating the vagus nerve directly — it's one of the fastest ways to flip the switch from sympathetic to parasympathetic.

Your body learns fast. Most people notice the pattern breaking within a week.

**Close line (bottom):**
Elemental Health & Nutrition

posts.on_image:
Slide 1 (hook frame — the entire reel cover):
"Viral infection isn't just acute. It can shift how your **immune** system tolerates thyroid tissue.

Post any infection (EBV, COVID, even a minor viral trigger), and some people's antibody response stays elevated — sometimes for months. This is the functional medicine angle: treating thyroid antibodies often means addressing the immune-tolerance piece, not just TSH.

Swipe to understand how."

(Note: This is a REEL HOOK — only the on-screen text is shown. The "swipe to understand" is the narrative bridge; if this is a multi-slide reel, subsequent slides expand. For a SINGLE-FRAME reel cover, keep on-screen text to 2–3 punchy lines max, and let the caption carry the story.

Headline: "Viral **immune** shift and thyroid"
Body: "Infection can reset your body's tolerance to thyroid tissue. Here's why that matters — and what functional medicine does differently."
posts.caption:
Viral infection and thyroid antibodies are deeply linked — and it's one reason a functional medicine approach looks beyond TSH alone.

When your body fights a viral infection (EBV, COVID, or even a stubborn respiratory virus), your immune system is working hard. Occasionally, especially after repeat or chronic activation, that immune response can become overactive toward your own tissues — including your thyroid.

The research is clear: people with a history of viral reactivation (or post-viral sequelae) often show elevated thyroid peroxidase (TPO) and thyroglobulin antibodies. Your conventional doctor might see elevated antibodies and focus on hormone replacement. A functional medicine lens asks: *what shifted the immune tolerance in the first place?* 

That's where we look at viral triggers, gut integrity, and hidden drivers of immune dysregulation. Treating the antibody piece often means resolving the underlying infection story — not just managing the thyroid symptoms.

If you've had a viral illness followed by unexplained fatigue, brain fog, or temperature sensitivity, thyroid antibody testing might be worth exploring.

Ready to dig deeper? Book a consultation with us.

#ThyroidHealth #FunctionalMedicine #AutoimmuneThyroid #ViralTriggers #GutHealth

posts.on_image:
HEADLINE: "Why [*Testing*] Matters Before the Supplements"

BODY:
One of my patients walked in convinced she had a "broken MTHFR gene." She'd read about methylation online, bought a genetic test from a wellness site, saw one variant flagged, and started a regimen of methylfolate and B12. Within days: heart palpitations, anxiety, and insomnia.

Here's what she didn't know: MTHFR is just one gene in a complex pathway. A variant doesn't mean broken. And jumping straight to supplementation without baseline homocysteine, methylmalonic acid, or folate levels? That's like refilling a tank without knowing if it's already full.

The conversation around MTHFR online has become so fear-filled that people are treating it as a diagnosis. It's not. It's a genetic variation—many of us carry them.

What matters is testing first: blood work, dietary history, symptom patterns. Only then can we see if methylation support is even needed, and at what dose.

If you've felt panicked by a genetic result or wondered whether you actually need those expensive methylated supplements, you're not alone. That's exactly why we explore this in clinical context, not algorithm context.

Reply if you'd like to dig into what your results actually mean.

Elemental Health & Nutrition
